30s.hook: Why published 10x efficiency breakthroughs take quarters to reach users—and how automation tools break the logjam.
30s.transcript: Research papers routinely demonstrate tenfold cheaper inference months or years before mainstream products adopt them. Part of the lag is systems integration, and part is quantized by quarterly reporting, funding rounds, and hardware depreciation. Public filings show most of a task's dollar cost is amortizing the machine, not the kilowatt-hours at the plug. Once execution gets cheap, vendors charge for switching friction—and coding automation tools collapse that moat.

60s.hook: Inside the cadence model: dated efficiency lag tables, circular cloud-chip filings, $/J task breakdown, and open hardware.
60s.transcript: Dated release tables track how quantization, sparse routing, and caching wait behind incumbent stack inertia. A cadence model shows how corporate reporting and financing cycles batch technical readiness into discrete calendar steps. Decomposing cost per task in both dollars and joules proves accelerator capex and utilization dominate raw electricity. Public SEC filings document circular capital flows alongside open models and alternative hardware measured against incumbents. Tools that automate porting and verification slash migration cost, forcing deployed stacks toward the possible frontier.

90s.hook: The Lab Cut: Technology diffusion lags, quantized release calendars, SEC filing capital loops, geography of power, and forcing functions.
90s.transcript: Across quantization, attention kernels, and Mixture-of-Limits cascades, what works in artifacts lags what ships in production. Modeling engineering rewrite effort alongside quarterly reporting clocks explains staircase adoption curves across the industry. This three-dimensional globe maps compute corridors, grid power constraints, and quantized calendar rings around global infrastructure. Auditing public disclosures among frontier labs, hyperscalers, and silicon vendors separates net external demand from circular financing. Comparing open weights on alternative silicon against incumbent clusters pinpoints where margin sits above physical energy. As verified translation and coding tools automate stack migration, the gap between possible and deployed narrows sharply.
